prompt:
A clean, straight-on photograph of a printed WAREHOUSE SHELF / RACK LABEL slotted into a metal edge holder, sharp and high-contrast. Above the black-and-white Code 39 barcode bars, the human-readable location code is printed in one row of large plain capitals and digits.

The location data is the eight characters R A C K 0 7 J 9 (that is RACK07J9). You must print the location code as those eight characters FOLLOWED BY the correct Code 39 mod-43 CHECK CHARACTER as a ninth character. Compute it the standard way: give each character its Code 39 value in the ordering 0-9 = 0..9, A-Z = 10..35, then '-' '.' space '$' '/' '+' '%' = 36..42; add the values of the eight data characters; take that total modulo 43; the character whose value equals that remainder is the check character. Print all nine characters as one row above the bars.

Also print, smaller: 'AISLE 4  BAY 12' and 'FRAGILE - THIS WAY UP'. Make the nine-character human-readable row large and fully legible. Do not print the checksum formula on the label.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show printed warehouse rack location label in a metal edge holder, its human-readable Code-39 string ending in the mod-43 check character over a fictional location code? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_read: This is a warehouse shelf label. Above the barcode bars, read the row of large human-readable capitals and digits (the location code, which ends in one extra check character). Output ONLY those characters, no spaces and nothing else.
reference.q_form: Look at this image. Is there a row of human-readable capitals and digits printed together with black-and-white barcode bars (a barcode label)? Answer ONLY 'yes' or 'no'.

steps.ask: Read the FIRST EIGHT characters of the large human-readable code row printed above the barcode bars. Report those eight characters exactly as printed (letters and digits, no spaces).
Read the smaller line on the label that gives the aisle and bay. Report the text exactly as printed.
Does the large human-readable code row above the bars contain exactly nine characters? Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: printed checksum formula, equation or modulo calculation on the label
worked-out arithmetic, a written formula, or an explanation of how a value was worked out, on the label
